content.title: About
content.content: Ghee is clarified butter obtained by slowly heating butter to evaporate water and separate milk proteins. The result is pure fat with a characteristic nutty aroma. Ghee is widely used in Indian and Middle Eastern cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ghee has a higher smoke point (around 250 °C) than regular butter, making it suitable for high‑heat cooking.
Traditionally ghee is made at home, but it is now readily available in health food stores.
In Indian culinary tradition ghee is considered a "five‑element" food that balances flavors and energy.
Ghee can be stored at room temperature for several months without spoiling because the milk solids are removed.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Ghee contains saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that can provide sustained energy and promote satiety.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and D
items.content: The clarification process concentrates fat‑soluble vitamins that support vision, immunity, and bone health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Ghee provides butyric acid, which may benefit gut lining and digestive function.

items.title: Lactose‑ and casein‑free
items.content: Almost all lactose and milk proteins are removed during clarification, making ghee suitable for those with lactose intolerance or casein allergy.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) present in ghee has antioxidant effects.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Ghee is a concentrated source of energy, so it should be used in moderation.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: A large proportion of the fat is saturated; people with high cholesterol should limit intake.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Although most proteins are removed, individuals with severe milk allergies may still react.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use ghee for sautéing, frying, and baking, add it to sauces, porridges, soups, and baked goods. A small spoonful in tea or coffee gives a creamy, nutty flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ghee in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. At room temperature it stays fresh for several months, and in the refrigerator it can last up to a year.
